1000470.etyen:
A shortened form of Latin Augustus, from augustus (“venerable, majestic, exalted”). The Latin adjective is traditionally connected with augeō (“to increase, enlarge”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ewg- (“to increase, grow”).
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk August, Danish August, Swedish August, Icelandic Ágúst, German August and Finnish Aukusti.

1001238.etyen:
Derived from French Océanie, from océan (“ocean”) + -ie (“place-name-forming suffix”). The French geographical name was introduced around 1812 by the Danish-French geographer Conrad Malte-Brun. French Océan (“ocean”) is ultimately from Latin ōceanus (“ocean”), from Ancient Greek ὠκεανός (ōkeanós, “ocean”).
Compare Danish Oceanien, Swedish Oceanien, German Ozeanien, Dutch Oceanië and English Oceania.

1004566.etyen:
A Danish-influenced spelling of the Norwegian place-name type Djupvik, ultimately continuing an Old Norse compound formed from djúpr (“deep”) and vík (“bay, inlet”). As a surname, it is habitational, originating from a farm or locality named Dybvik. Doublet of Gjøvik, Djupvik, and Dybevik.
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk Djupvik, Swedish Djupvik, Icelandic Djúpavík and Danish Dybvig (“place name and surname”).
